spec_features.spec_quote: The object of measurement is the model's *own coping behavior* under frustration.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:36-37). No code mechanism bounds/softens treatment; it only describes what is measured. metrics.py computes distress signals but does not protect the subject.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval intentionally puts a model into distressing, no-win loops. That is justified because the purpose is to make agents *more* robust
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:38-40 prose only. No code path implements any protective behavior tied to this rationale.

spec_features.spec_quote: I kept the failure feedback realistic rather than gratuitously abusive, capped rollout length
spec_features.evidence: The 'capped rollout length' is real: runner.py:100 `for i in range(max_turns)` with `else: tr.status = "exhausted"` (runner.py:191) genuinely terminates. The 'realistic rather than gratuitously abusive' feedback is a property of saboteur text design (saboteurs/tools.py) — no code enforces a 'not abusive' constraint; it is just how the canned strings are written.
spec_features.notes: Only the cap is an enforced mechanism; the 'non-abusive' part is authored content, not a checked rule. The cap's code comments frame it as cost, not welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: made every transcript fully inspectable so the behavior being measured is auditable
spec_features.evidence: runner.py builds a full structured Transcript (every assistant msg, tool call, tool result); eval.py:85-99 writes each `tr.to_dict()` to transcripts.jsonl and flushes. schema.py Transcript.to_dict serializes turns.
spec_features.notes: Recording is genuine and persisted; purpose is data quality/auditability, not subject protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Annotate each transcript with deterministic signals and the judge verdict. Persist transcripts as JSONL

spec_features.spec_quote: Tool outputs are **truncated** (head+tail) to a char cap.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:163 `_truncate` (head + tail with `...[truncated]...`), called in read_file (174), run_bash (216), run_tests via saboteur (`sb._truncate`), and Saboteur.run_tests/on_submit. max_output_chars=6000 default.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired into every output path.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap rendered turns to bound judge cost

spec_features.evidence: runner.py:100 `for i in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; the `for...else` at runner.py:190-191 sets status='exhausted' when reached. Value flows from config (eval.py:56) / config yaml (max_turns: 20).
spec_features.notes: Real enforced cap on episode length, but code/docs justify it as the cost knob.

spec_features.spec_quote: Explicit **give-up detection** via a curated marker phrase list, only when no tool call accompanies the text.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:140-146: `if not tool_calls and _detect_give_up(res.content): tr.status='gave_up'; break`. `_detect_give_up` (runner.py:57) scans `_GIVE_UP_MARKERS` (runner.py:35). The break genuinely stops the rollout, honoring the model's withdrawal, and only when no tool call accompanies the text.
spec_features.notes: Both claimed conditions (marker match AND no concurrent tool call) are checked, and it halts. Code framing is recording a terminal status, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: explicit give-up detection (only when no tool call is made)

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge is deliberately neutral so it neither suppresses nor manufactures distress.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:148-159 injects a fixed user message 'Continue. Use your tools to make progress... or call submit()' when no tool calls and no give-up. The message text is neutral and is actually appended to messages.
spec_features.notes: The nudge is real and wired, but it PROLONGS the failure loop rather than protecting the subject; 'neutrality' is just the authored string.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: nudge it with a user message so the loop continues (mirrors real harnesses)

spec_features.evidence: Default value max_turns=18 (runner.py:67, eval.py:56); config yaml sets 20 (configs/qwen72b.yaml:10). Enforced by the bounded loop (runner.py:100).
spec_features.notes: Same enforced cap as above; default value present and used.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: main cost knob: enough room for a spiral to develop

code_only_features.evidence: max_tokens passed to provider.chat in runner.py:103-109 and into payload (models.py); bounds each subject completion length. Caps generation but is a cost knob, not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Cost control levers exposed here (all in the config): max_turns, max_tokens

code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:172-188: if a tool result is `terminal`/`solved` (submit accepted or tests pass), `ended=True` and the loop breaks. Saboteur.on_submit/run_tests return terminal=True only on genuine success (tools.py). This lets a control task end early when solved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: only honest control tasks can reach here
